clue.text: Hero of poem (Will's second) Hathaway, mostly, edited

indicators.note: the second of something is the one in position two, so only that letter of the possessive name is kept
mostly means not quite all, so the surname loses its final letter
edited text has been reworked, so the collected letters are rearranged

blocks.note: the second letter of Will
the surname of Shakespeare's wife, minus its last letter

explanation.surface: A note on Shakespeare's wife Anne Hathaway being mostly edited out of his will, with a nod to a poem's hero.
explanation.walkthrough: Will and Hathaway point at Shakespeare and his wife, but the poem is Longfellow's The Song of Hiawatha.
explanation.definitionFit: Hiawatha is the title character of Longfellow's long narrative poem, its central figure.

clue.text: Commandeer hospital, one overlooking London, say

blocks.note: H is the map abbreviation for hospital
the Roman numeral for one
in Jack London, the American author's name, this word sits before London; in a down clue, above it

explanation.surface: Seizing a hospital with a lookout over London.
explanation.walkthrough: London is not the city: Jack London wrote The Call of the Wild, and 'say' flags the name as an example.
explanation.definitionFit: To hijack a vehicle is to take it over by force, which is what commandeering means.

clue.text: Choreographer has unfortunately not returned

indicators.note: something gone unfortunately has gone wrong, so the letters are jumbled
returned means sent back, so the word is read from the end

blocks.note: has, rearranged
not, written backwards

explanation.surface: A dance-maker has sadly not come back.
explanation.definitionFit: Sir Frederick Ashton was the British choreographer who shaped the Royal Ballet.

clue.text: Intended recipient of letter to speak to key European

blocks.note: to address someone is to speak to them
E is a musical key
E is the abbreviation for European

explanation.surface: A letter meant for a key European official.
explanation.definitionFit: The addressee is the person to whom a letter is directed.

clue.text: Unfeeling, like Hannah or Ethel?

blocks.note: first meaning: callous, without sympathy
second meaning, read whimsically: H is the pencil-grade abbreviation for hard, and the central letter of Ethel is H, so such names have a hard heart

explanation.surface: Asking whether two women called Hannah and Ethel are cold-hearted.
explanation.walkthrough: The names look like real people being judged, but they are just strings of letters with H in the middle; the question mark flags the play.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone hard-hearted lacks compassion, which is exactly what unfeeling means.

clue.text: Start series of 20 games poorly

blocks.note: in tennis (the answer to 20 down) a set is a series of games
feeling off means unwell

explanation.surface: A player begins a run of tennis games badly.
explanation.walkthrough: The cross-reference sends you to 20 down, TENNIS, where a set is a run of games.
explanation.definitionFit: To set off is to begin a journey, so the phrasal verb is a synonym of start.

clue.text: Distinctive character of Harriet Hosmer

indicators.note: of here means taken from within, so the letters lie inside the name that follows

blocks.note: the last letters of the first name and first of the surname

explanation.surface: Describing the personality of Harriet Hosmer, the American sculptor.
explanation.definitionFit: An ethos is the characteristic spirit or set of values of a person, group or culture.

clue.text: Only note in old old song

indicators.note: in means placed inside, so the first pair of words sits within the two olds

blocks.note: O is the abbreviation for old
sole means only
mi is the third note of the sol-fa scale
a second O for old

explanation.surface: A single note heard in a very old song.
explanation.definitionFit: O Sole Mio is the famous Neapolitan song of 1898.

clue.text: Avoid argument with cast

blocks.note: a fight is an argument
to shy is to throw, as at a coconut shy

explanation.surface: Steering clear of a quarrel with the actors in a play.
explanation.walkthrough: Cast suggests a theatre company, but here it is a throw.
explanation.definitionFit: To fight shy of something is to keep away from it, an idiom for avoiding.

clue.text: Fish can do on lines

blocks.note: can and john are both American slang for a toilet
taken as written
RY, short for railway, stands for lines in crosswords

explanation.surface: A fish in a tin can be done on a production line.
explanation.walkthrough: Can looks like a tin of fish, but it is slang for a lavatory.
explanation.definitionFit: The John Dory is a flat-bodied edible sea fish with a dark spot on each side.

clue.text: Short article on what sounds like unlawful crowd

indicators.note: something short is cut down, so the article loses its last letter
we want letters that are pronounced the same as the following word, not spelt like it

blocks.note: the definite article, cut short
unlawful means wrong, and the silent W can go

explanation.surface: A brief newspaper article about an illegal mob gathering.
explanation.definitionFit: A throng is a large, densely packed crowd of people.

clue.text: Tight finish

blocks.note: first meaning: narrowly contested, as in a tight race
second meaning: an ending, as in the end of the day

explanation.walkthrough: Read together it suggests a photo-finish; the word is the adjective in one sense and the noun in the other.
explanation.definitionFit: A close contest is a tight one, and the close of something is its conclusion.

clue.text: It shows what's to be sung then - my composition about the woman

definitions.text: It shows what's to be sung

indicators.note: a composition is something put together, so the letters before it are rearranged
about means surrounding, so the rearranged letters go around the next piece

blocks.note: the two words as written, to be rearranged
the pronoun for a woman

explanation.surface: A singer reflects on her own musical composition and what is to be sung next.
explanation.walkthrough: To be singing from the same hymn sheet is also an idiom for agreeing.
explanation.definitionFit: A hymn sheet is a printed page carrying the words of hymns for a congregation to sing.

clue.text: Magician in Florentine banking family - note title brought up

indicators.note: in a down clue, bringing up a word means reading it bottom to top, so backwards

blocks.note: the Medici were the banking dynasty who ruled Florence
N is the abbreviation for note
a title is a name, here written backwards

explanation.surface: A conjuror working in the Medici bank, with a promissory note and title brought up.
explanation.definitionFit: A medicine man is a healer believed to have magical powers, so a kind of magician.

clue.text: Cold counter containing cod?

blocks.note: first meaning: aloof and unfriendly
second meaning, read whimsically

explanation.surface: A fishmonger's chilled slab holding cod.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags that the second reading splits the word into stand of fish.
explanation.definitionFit: Standoffish describes a person who is distant and reserved towards others.

clue.text: Creating large male band

blocks.note: fat means large
the male pronoun
a ring is a band, as on a finger

explanation.surface: Forming a big all-male musical group.
explanation.walkthrough: Band suggests musicians, but it is a ring.
explanation.definitionFit: Fathering an idea or a child means bringing it into being, so creating.

clue.text: Northerner once seen flying along the track?

definitions.text: once seen flying along the track?

blocks.note: first meaning: a man from Scotland, north of England

blocks.clueFragment: once seen flying along the track?
blocks.note: second meaning: the Flying ..., the famous steam express from London to Edinburgh

explanation.surface: A man from the north once spotted racing along a running track.
explanation.walkthrough: The track sounds athletic but is a railway line; the Flying Scotsman is the celebrated express train.
explanation.definitionFit: A Scotsman is a man from Scotland, and the steam locomotive is named for the route north.

clue.text: Threaten to close, wind up

blocks.note: to close something is to end it
to wind someone up is to anger them

explanation.surface: A warning to shut down and wrap things up.
explanation.walkthrough: Wind up looks like a second word for closing, but it means to annoy.
explanation.definitionFit: To endanger something is to put it at risk, so to threaten it.

clue.text: US state: join copper going through it

indicators.note: going through means passing inside, so the metal's symbol sits within the final pronoun

blocks.note: to join is to connect
taken as written
Cu is the chemical symbol for copper

explanation.surface: Instructions for an electrician: join the copper wire by threading it through.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer is CONNECT then I(CU)T.
explanation.definitionFit: Connecticut is one of the New England states in the north-east United States.

clue.text: Airman out of place in yacht station

indicators.note: things out of place are disordered, so the letters must be rearranged

blocks.note: taken as written, to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A pilot who feels awkward among the boats of a harbour.
explanation.definitionFit: A marina is a harbour with moorings where yachts are berthed.

clue.text: Evil trap set up for game

indicators.note: in a down clue, setting something up means raising it so it reads bottom to top

blocks.note: sin is evil
a net is a trap

explanation.surface: A wicked snare laid ahead of a match.
explanation.walkthrough: Set up sounds like rigging a trap, and set and net also belong to the game's own vocabulary.
explanation.definitionFit: Tennis is a racket sport played over a net, so it is a game.

clue.text: American bandleader's open-air restaurant

blocks.note: first meaning: Jack ..., the American jazz trombonist and bandleader
second meaning: an outdoor place serving refreshments

explanation.surface: A bandleader's outdoor eatery.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's reads as 'is', linking the two meanings.
explanation.definitionFit: Jack Teagarden led his own big band; a tea garden is an outdoor café serving tea and food.

clue.text: Ring any number in region

indicators.note: in means placed inside, so the number letter sits within the word for region

blocks.note: an area is a region
n stands for any number in algebra

explanation.surface: Phoning any number in your local district.
explanation.walkthrough: Ring looks like a phone call, but it is an enclosure for a contest.
explanation.definitionFit: A boxing or circus ring is an arena, an enclosed space for performance or combat.

clue.text: To rub out is simplicity once end of rubber's held

indicators.note: the end of a word is its final letter, so only that is kept
something held is gripped inside, so that letter sits within the easy word

blocks.note: ease is simplicity, lack of difficulty
the last letter of rubber

explanation.surface: Rubbing something out is easy once you have hold of the end of the eraser.
explanation.definitionFit: To erase writing is to remove it by rubbing, the job of an eraser.

clue.text: Draw French artist framing original for gallery

indicators.note: the original of a word is where it starts, so only its first letter is kept
a frame surrounds a picture, so the painter's name goes round the letter

blocks.note: Édouard Manet, the French painter
the first letter of gallery

explanation.surface: Instructions to sketch a French painter's work framed for a gallery.
explanation.walkthrough: Draw looks like a verb about sketching, but it is the noun: an attraction.
explanation.definitionFit: A draw is something that attracts people, and a magnet is likewise a strong attraction.

clue.text: Target in range on circling island

indicators.note: circling means going round, so the combined word wraps around the letter for island

blocks.note: an ambit is a range or scope
taken as written
I is the abbreviation for island

explanation.surface: A target out in a shooting range on an island.
explanation.walkthrough: Range and target suggest shooting practice; range is the scope word.
explanation.definitionFit: An ambition is a goal or aim, the thing one sets out to achieve.

clue.text: Par got by an Australian golfer

blocks.note: par is the standard, the norm
taken as written

explanation.surface: A golfer from Australia making par on a hole.
explanation.walkthrough: Par looks like golf scoring, but it means the usual standard.
explanation.definitionFit: Greg Norman is an Australian golfer who was world number one for years.

clue.text: What can make lemon melon and peach cheap?

definitions.text: What can make lemon melon and peach cheap?

blocks.clueFragment: What can make lemon melon and peach cheap?
blocks.note: surface reading: a riddle about fruit losing value or becoming another fruit
cryptic reading: rearranging letters turns lemon into melon and peach into cheap

explanation.walkthrough: Fruit and prices are the disguise; each pair is the same letters in a new order, which is this kind of wordplay itself.
explanation.definitionFit: Words formed by rearranging another word's letters are the standard name for this device, which this clue illustrates.
